Package io.webagent4j.policy

Interface IExecutionPolicy<C>

Type Parameters:
C - the immutable context type this policy evaluates
All Known Subinterfaces:
IActionPolicy, INetworkPolicy
Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface IExecutionPolicy<C>
A synchronous, in-process authorization gate: given an immutable context C, decide whether the operation it describes may proceed.

Contract:

  • Synchronous only. Implementations must not block on network I/O, an MCP call, an LLM call, a database query, or any other remote round trip. Evaluation is expected to complete quickly and deterministically given its input.
  • Fail closed. evaluate(C) declares no checked exception, so an implementation can only ever throw an unchecked RuntimeException; a thrown RuntimeException, a returned null, or any other failure to produce a decision must be treated by the caller as if this method returned PolicyDecision.deny(io.webagent4j.policy.PolicyReason). This interface itself does not catch or translate exceptions and does not retry a failed evaluation - callers that invoke a policy in a governed pipeline are responsible for catching RuntimeException and null results exactly once per evaluation, without any hidden retry, so that any failure denies rather than silently allows. A fatal Error (for example OutOfMemoryError or StackOverflowError) is never part of this fail-closed contract: it must propagate uncaught, not be silently converted into a deny decision.
  • No hidden retry. An implementation must not retry the underlying decision itself; if it needs to consult something unreliable, that unreliability must be surfaced as an exception, not masked with a retry loop the caller cannot observe.
  • Two outcomes only. PolicyOutcome.ALLOW or PolicyOutcome.DENY - there is no way to express "ask a human" or "not sure yet" through this contract.
  • Untrusted, unsandboxed code. A caller-supplied implementation runs as ordinary Java code with no sandboxing. This framework guarantees it will not invoke a governed backend before a policy allows it, but it cannot prevent or undo side effects a malicious or buggy policy implementation performs itself during evaluation.
